title: Accounting Concepts, Principles & Financial Statement Elements

stages.scenario: Acquired commercial property for ₹50,00,000, incurring ₹5,00,000 for structural elevation and ₹5,00,000 in statutory registration levies. At year-end, current market appraisal reaches ₹70,00,000.
stages.question: At what capitalized value should this property be recorded on the Balance Sheet?

options.text: Record at ₹60,00,000 (Historical Acquisition Cost + Improvement + Legal/Registration)
options.feedback: Correct! Under the Historical Cost Concept, fixed assets are recorded at purchase price plus all direct costs necessary to bring the asset into operational use. Subsequent market escalation is not recognized.
Incorrect. Revaluation to market value on initial carry violates the Historical Cost Concept.

stages.scenario: A client submits a commercial fire insurance proposal on March 30 for ₹5,00,000 annual premium. The risk proposal is accepted immediately, but the premium payment instrument is received and cleared on April 6.
stages.question: When does statutory revenue recognition occur for this transaction?

options.text: Recognize on April 6 when the premium instrument is actually received and cleared
options.feedback: Correct! Under statutory insurance premium realization rules (Section 64VB), premium revenue and risk coverage are legally operative only upon actual receipt of premium.

options.text: Recognize on March 30 under general trade accrual since the proposal was accepted
options.feedback: Incorrect. In insurance accounting, statutory premium collection mandates supersede standard mercantile accrual.

stages.scenario: Apex Shield settles an outstanding fire loss liability of ₹1,00,00,000 via direct banking transfer.
stages.question: How does this settlement impact the fundamental accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity)?

options.text: Decrease Current Assets (Bank) by ₹1 Cr; Decrease Current Liabilities (Outstanding Claims) by ₹1 Cr
options.feedback: Correct! Dual Aspect maintains parity: a reduction in liability is matched with an equal reduction in assets, leaving net equity unchanged.

options.text: Decrease Bank by ₹1 Cr; Decrease Equity by ₹1 Cr
options.feedback: Incorrect. Outstanding claims were already charged as an incurred expense when intimated. The actual cash settlement reduces existing liabilities, not equity.

stages.scenario: Total annual sales/earned revenue is ₹10,000. Purchases are ₹5,000, wages/salaries paid are ₹2,000 with ₹1,000 accrued/outstanding at year-end, and commission paid is ₹1,000 (which includes ₹500 prepaid for the subsequent period).
stages.question: Applying the Matching Concept, what is the net operational profit?

options.feedback: Correct! Matching requires matching incurred expenses against earned revenue: Purchases (₹5,000) + Incurred Wages (₹2,000 + ₹1,000) + Incurred Commission (₹1,000 - ₹500) = ₹8,500 expenses. Profit = ₹1,500.
Incorrect. Taking only cash paid (₹8,000) ignores accrued liabilities and prepaid deductions, distorting true periodic profit.

stages.scenario: Year-end inventory of salvage goods has a historical cost of ₹1,50,000, but changing market demand drops its Net Realizable Value (NRV) to ₹1,10,000.
stages.question: At what valuation must the inventory be carried on the financial statements?

options.text: ₹1,10,000 (Lower of Cost or Net Realizable Value, recognizing ₹40,000 diminution loss immediately)
options.feedback: Correct! Under the Prudence principle, anticipated losses are recognized immediately, and inventory is valued at lower of cost or NRV.

options.text: ₹1,50,000 (Retain at Historical Cost until actual cash disposal occurs)
options.feedback: Incorrect. Retaining historical cost overstates asset values and violates the prudence convention.
